extracted.intended_audience: regional TV creatives and producers seeking to pitch ideas to Channel 4 commissioners (West Midlands creatives)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creatives preparing to meet Channel 4 commissioning editors — what kinds of shows they commission and how to use short networking/1-2-1 opportunities. Focuses on factual entertainment, specialist factual (science/adventure), documentaries and entertainment/live formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel 4 genre remit
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel 4 commissions across reality, factual entertainment, specialist factual (science & adventure), entertainment & live, and documentaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists commissioners whose slates cover reality, gameshows, comedy entertainment, live, specialist factual (science & adventure), and documentaries — use these genres to determine programme fit. Examples on the page include The Apprentice, Rise & Fall, Grand Designs, Late Night Lycett, The Last Leg, SAS output, and First Dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel-defining reality ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Steven Handley is “particularly keen to hear about channel-defining reality ideas, with real noise and scale & one-off big scale celebrity led access ideas.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch reality formats that feel bold/scalable and can create cultural ‘noise’; celebrity-led access concepts and one-off large-scale ideas are explicitly highlighted. Relevant slate credits: Late Night Lycett, The Last Leg, Jimmy Carr’s I Literally Just Told You, Tempting Fortune.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual entertainment (high-volume/show formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cal Turner commissions factual entertainment and has helped bring high-volume reality shows like Rise & Fall to screens; his background includes working across formats such as The Apprentice, Snowflake Mountain, Grand Designs, and 60 Days with Ed Stafford.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target tried-and-tested factual entertainment formats or high-volume reality concepts that can sustain series runs. Emphasise format hooks and audience appeal demonstrated by existing credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialist factual — science & adventure
rubrics_metrics.description: Jonah Weston (Commissioner for Science and Adventure in Specialist Factual) looks after SAS output, Guy Martin’s adventures and a diverse range of shows including Hollywood Heist: The Bling Ring, Super Surgeons, 2022: The Year From Space, The Academy, and What Killed the Whale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch ideas grounded in science, exploration or adventure with strong practical/experiential hooks and identifiable talent or missions. Demonstrate how the idea fits the specialist factual remit (e.g., high-adrenaline adventure series, space/science access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Talent-fronted and first-time director opportunities (documentaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Janine Thomas commissions First Cut (a strand giving first time factual directors their first terrestrial hour), looks after talent-fronted documentaries and returning series such as First Dates, 24 Hours in A&E and Night Coppers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary pitches can be talent-fronted or suitable for First Cut (emerging directors). Highlight storytelling voice, talent attachments, and suitability as a single film or returning series. Cite relevant comparable shows when describing format and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme slate credibility (use commissioner credits as exemplars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioners’ slates are cited (e.g., The Apprentice, Grand Designs, Rise & Fall, SAS output, Guy Martin projects, Late Night Lycett, First Dates, 24 Hours in A&E) indicating the types of projects they greenlight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the commissioners’ past credits to position your idea: show how it relates to or differentiates from existing Channel 4 shows, and which commissioner’s remit it best aligns with. Demonstrate commercial/creative fit and comparable audience propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared for short 1-to-1 pitch slots
rubrics_metrics.description: Networking opportunities included a chance to schedule 15-minute 1-2-1s with the four commissioning editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a concise, structured 15-minute pitch: clear logline, format, audience, what makes it distinctive, and any talent attachments or proof of concept. Bring one-page materials or visuals and be ready to answer commissioning-focused questions; use the meeting to build relationships and gain content-strategy insight.
